nodes.plm_action: Remove small cap by pushing screwdriver tip into clip
nodes.plm_caption:
A person's hands are shown taking a black round cover off of a cord and then using a tool to try and fix the cord. The video is in slow motion.
A person's left hand can be seen at the bottom left corner and then lifting the black circular cover off of a black cord. The person's hand then holds the cover on the right side. The hand on the left comes from the bottom left corner and is gripping the black cord that goes under the circular cover. It is held in the person's right hand. The hand picks up the circular cover and flips it on the other side showing that there is a clear plastic circle at the center of it. He then places the cover down. The hand on the right lifts the clear plastic circle off of the cover and shows the metal piece at the center. He points at a wire coming off of the plastic circle and then uses his hand to lift the cord. The hand lifts up a screwdriver, and points at the cord. He then uses his hand to carefully grab a needle shaped metal object that is connected to the cord. He moves the object in several directions and pushes and pulls on the cord. The focus is on the hands and the cord. The camera stays on the hands and cord throughout the entire video.  A black wall can be seen on the right side, with shadows of the hand and cord visible on the surface.

summary.brief: Removing a floor‑lamp foot switch and releasing its hot wire.
summary.detailed: The hands grasp the foot switch assembly on a floor lamp and begin by unscrewing three of the four mounting screws with a screwdriver, then remove the last screw to free the front cover. The front plate is lifted off, leaving the button in place, and turned upside‑down to expose the internal mechanism, including a spring and the single hot‑side wire that is switched. The lower half of the housing is also opened to show how the hot conductor wraps around a metal clip. Using a tiny screwdriver from an eyeglass‑repair kit, the tip is inserted into a release hole in the clip; the pressure releases the grip on the crimped copper‑sleeved wire, which is then pulled out of the switch. The same release procedure is performed on the opposite side, demonstrating how the switch can be completely removed and later reinstalled by reversing these steps.

action.detailed: Unscrew the mounting screws, lift off the front cover, flip it to expose the interior, press the release hole with a tiny screwdriver to disengage the crimped hot wire, and pull the wire out, repeating the release on the opposite side.

A small black box on the left of the frame.

summary.brief: A white tray filled with assorted tools is shown while a finger from the left briefly touches a black component and then the hand moves a black cord on the tray.
summary.detailed: The camera opens on an open white tray or box that holds several tools—a yellow‑handled screwdriver, a black button‑like part attached to a long black cord, a thin tube, a circular black rubber piece with a hole, and other silver tools—plus a small black box visible on the left side. A finger enters from the left edge, presses the black tool, casting a shadow beneath it, and then the hand slides or repositions the black cord/wire across the tray. The scene remains otherwise static.

action.detailed: Press the finger onto the black tool on the tray and then slide the attached black cord, repositioning it on the surface.

nodes.plm_action: Unscrewing the switch
nodes.plm_caption: This is a first person view of the contents of an electrical kit. The lighting is bright, but the camera is somewhat unfocused. The individual starts by looking at a black circular component with wires protruding from either side of the middle. He points to the two wires, picks up the circular part, and flips it over, revealing a hole in the middle, a black wire with a silver tip and a clear plastic piece. He holds the clear plastic piece up, tilts it forward and shows it to the camera. He picks up a small silver cylindrical object, sticks it into the clear plastic piece and unscrews it with the included Allen key and turns the clear plastic piece and the small silver object around. It is not clear if he is trying to fit the clear piece into the silver object or if he is just rotating it. The camera remains focused on his hands, not the kit contents, though it is possible that he is either reassembling or disassembling the kit. The light in the background is overexposed and is rather visible than useful for the video. The light sources are most likely coming from the camera. The scene is static, with little, if any, movement.

summary.brief: The presenter disassembles a floor‑lamp foot switch, exposing its internal momentary‑contact mechanism and wiring.
summary.detailed: In a first‑person view, the demonstrator points to the two wires on the black circular foot switch, unscrews three of the four mounting screws with a small screwdriver, lifts off the front plate, and flips the switch assembly over to reveal a spring‑loaded momentary‑contact switch. He distinguishes the hot side (the copper‑sleeved wire) from the neutral side, inserts the screwdriver tip into the release hole to free the wire clamp, pulls the hot wire out of the switch, and removes the remaining components, setting them aside as preparation for installing a new foot switch.

action.detailed: Unscrew the visible screws, lift off the black cover, insert the screwdriver into the release hole to disengage the wire clamp, and pull the copper‑sleeved hot wire out of the switch.

An array of tools such as a screwdriver, a black button and a thin tube are shown. They are on a white tray. One tool has a long black piece attached to it. There is a rubber stopper at one end, and a screw at the other.
The items are still.

nodes.plm_action: Removing the plastic cover by turning it counterclockwise
nodes.plm_caption:
This video features a close up of a person's hands holding a black cable and cover from a tool in a white box. The person points to screws, then shows the inside of the cover by pulling it out and the clip pointing to the inside before they push the clip out. The person then holds the wires in the left hand while the right holds the silver clip out and between his finger.
The background is a grey floor and a black wall.

summary.brief: The hands unscrew and remove the black plastic cover of a foot‑switch, expose the switch mechanism, and pull out the internal metal spring/clip while showing the wires.
summary.detailed: Beginning with a black round cover attached to a cord, the presenter points to the two screws that hold it, inserts a small screwdriver and turns the screws out. The cover is lifted off, flipped over and set aside, revealing a momentary‑contact switch inside. A metal spring‑loaded clip attached to the switch is then pushed out, held between the fingers, and the attached hot and neutral wires are displayed and separated. The clip is fully removed, completing the disassembly of the switch’s internal components.

action.brief: Disassemble foot‑switch cover and extract internal spring
action.detailed: Use a screwdriver to remove the two screws securing the black plastic cover, lift and flip the cover to expose the switch, then pull out the metal spring/clip while holding the wires with the other hand.

nodes.plm_action: Remove wire from old valve to new one
nodes.plm_caption:
The video shows a person's hands taking apart and fixing some kind of a black cable with a connector on the top.  They use a screwdriver to loosen some wires, and then take it apart.

The video is set against a blue carpet background with a white box containing some black plastic parts of the object in question on top.  There is also a screwdriver with a clear plastic handle in the white box.

No sound.

summary.brief: Hands disassemble a black foot‑switch assembly with a tiny screwdriver.
summary.detailed: The video shows a pair of hands lifting off the front plate of a black foot‑switch, exposing the internal mechanism. A very small screwdriver is inserted into a release slot on the connector and pressed to free the wire‑gripping wedge. The copper‑sleeved wire is then pulled out of the housing. The same screwdriver is used to turn a set‑screw counter‑clockwise, allowing the plastic insert that holds the spring to be removed along with the spring itself. With the cover, wire, spring and plastic insert separated, the switch housing is left empty, ready for a new foot‑switch to be installed.

action.detailed: Insert the tiny screwdriver into the release slot, press to release the wire‑grip, pull the wire out, then turn the set‑screw counter‑clockwise to detach the plastic insert and spring, separating all components of the switch.

nodes.plm_action: Remove screws from motor housing
nodes.plm_caption: A person’s hands are shown picking up a small black plastic piece and demonstrating how to remove it. Then, they use a screwdriver to unscrew a larger black piece which is then removed with their left hand. They hold it up in front of the camera and put it down into a white plastic case. Then they unscrew another part in the same spot until it too is removed. The video is set on top of a gray surface with a white plastic case behind the objects being shown. The lighting is focused on the objects.

summary.brief: Hands disassemble a foot‑switch assembly and expose its internal components.
summary.detailed: The demonstrator first picks up and removes a small black plastic cover from the foot‑switch. Using a screwdriver, a larger black housing is unscrewed; the left hand lifts this piece, holds it up for inspection, and places it into a white plastic case on the gray work surface. A second screw in the same location is turned and that part is also removed and stored in the case. Finally, the front plate is lifted off, the inner piece is turned upside‑down, revealing the momentary‑contact switch, spring and wiring inside the foot‑switch.

action.detailed: Remove the small plastic cover, unscrew the black housing with a screwdriver, place the removed parts into the white case, then lift off the front plate and turn the inner piece to expose the internal switch and spring.
action.actor: The demonstrator’s hands (the person performing the demonstration)

At the end, the man pulls out one of the different parts that the person was holding and looks at it.

summary.brief: The presenter removes the spring from a black foot‑switch, shows its wiring, then turns a motor base and demonstrates the two connected wires.
summary.detailed: The video begins with the presenter’s hands holding a black circular foot‑switch; he lifts off the metal spring that surrounds the central screw, revealing the cord that passes through the opening and the two wires attached to the switch. He points to the wires and the small screw while the interior of the switch is displayed. The hands then move to a motor base attached to the lamp, rotating the base to expose its underside. He presses the two wires with his thumb and forefinger, pulls them to illustrate the connections, lifts the base upward, rotates it back toward the camera, and finally pulls the motor assembly away, ending the segment.

action.brief: Disassemble foot switch and inspect motor base
action.detailed: Remove the spring from the black foot‑switch, expose its internal screw and wires, then rotate the motor base, press and pull its two wires, and lift the base away to show the connections.

nodes.plm_caption:
The video shows a person disassembling a machine, which appears to be a dehumidifier of some type. At the beginning, the machine is on the side, with tools and other parts on it. A black wire with a clear connector is held in the person's hand. They point out a metal ring and then stick a thermometer into the wire. They remove the ring and insert a needle that is bent over at the tip.
The person then turns the machine over and continues the process.
There is a black rubber mat or table mat visible on the right of the screen.

summary.brief: The presenter disassembles a foot‑switch, probes its contacts, and re‑attaches the black cord with a screw using a tiny probe and an Allen key.
summary.detailed: The segment opens with the presenter holding a black wire that ends in a clear connector and pointing out a metal ring on the switch housing. A bent metal needle is inserted into the connector while the unit is turned over. The presenter then turns the device upright, uses his thumb to locate a small black component on the switch and pokes the contacts with a tiny metal probe that fits into a black plastic cup. A pen with a transparent tube is used to press a small internal part, and a tiny metal spike is placed into the cup for further manipulation. Later, a screwdriver/Allen‑key is used to loosen the retaining screw that secures the cord, the wire is wiggled and pulled out of the switch, a new screw is placed on the cord end, and the screw is tightened to lock the connection. Throughout the segment only the hands and the small electrical parts are visible against a neutral carpeted background.

action.brief: Disassemble and resecure the switch wiring
action.detailed: Using a tiny metal probe and an Allen‑key, loosen the retaining screw on the black cord, pull the wire out of the foot‑switch, insert a new screw onto the cord end, and tighten it to lock the connection.

nodes.plm_action: Insert wire through connector body
nodes.plm_caption: This video features a pair of hands, holding a wiring harness and performing repairs by unscrewing a screw in it. The hands are shown making small movements in closeup from a top down perspective. There is a screwdriver resting at the right center.

summary.brief: Hands disassemble a small electrical connector, remove its wire and tube, and then re‑secure the assembly with a screw and nut.
summary.detailed: The video begins with the right hand holding a black wire while the left hand grips a clear plastic connector; a small screw is driven into the plastic cylinder and the wire is pulled out of the connector. The rubber‑capped metal tube is then unscrewed from its plastic housing and the black wire is extracted from the tube with needle‑nose pliers. The connector is lifted for inspection, a tiny screw is placed into the plug, and the wire is repeatedly inserted into and withdrawn from a tool. The black wire is fitted onto a metal device, and the ends of the wire are twisted inside the clear plastic parts, after which the clear pieces are removed with a screwdriver tip. A small silver nut is positioned over the wires, pressed between thumb and finger, and rotated clockwise onto the threaded portion of a silver switch with a black knob, which is moved up and down. The segment ends with the hand holding a small silver component with a black cord and pointing it toward a round fitting.

action.detailed: Unscrew the rubber‑capped metal tube from its plastic housing, pull the black wire out with needle‑nose pliers, drive a small screw into the clear plastic connector, and then press a small nut onto the threaded part of the switch and rotate it clockwise while adjusting the wire.

nodes.plm_action: Remove screws that secure top cover to wall switch box
nodes.plm_caption:
The video shows a man preparing to take apart a black plastic object on a white, plastic tool kit.
He holds the black plastic object in both hands. They are tools on the right of the screen are a flathead screwdriver with a yellow handle and clear handle. To the left are a two small screws and an orange-labeled vial. The man removes a plastic ring from the object.
He then grabs a black-handled screwdriver and points out that it has a yellow plastic handle.
The video is a good example of how a tool kit will help someone to remove or work on an object.

summary.brief: The presenter disassembles a black foot‑switch, removing its outer ring and screws to expose the internal mechanism.
summary.detailed: The presenter picks up the black round foot‑switch from the white tray and rotates it to examine it. He removes the plastic retaining ring and points to the cord attached to the switch, tapping a screw in the centre and pulling the cord slightly. Using a flat‑head screwdriver with a yellow handle, he unscrews three of the four screws that hold the front plate, lifts the plate off and flips the switch upside‑down, revealing a spring and contact pieces inside. He then switches to a small screwdriver with a black handle (yellow plastic tip) and unscrews a tiny nut on the metal part of the switch, further exposing the internal components. The camera remains focused on his hands throughout the process.

action.detailed: Unscrew the outer plastic ring and the front‑plate screws, lift the plate, turn the switch upside‑down, and then use the small screwdriver to remove the internal nut, exposing the mechanism.

nodes.plm_action: Open top cover and look at the wires attached
nodes.plm_caption: This video shows a person holding and working with small electronic components. They are manipulating the components with their hands, and a screwdriver is visible in the background. The video seems to be focused on assembling or repairing small electronic devices.

summary.brief: The front cover of a black foot‑switch is lifted off and the internal components are revealed.
summary.detailed: The hands grasp the black circular foot‑switch housing, press the button to release the front plate, lift the plate away and turn the housing upside‑down.  Inside the case a momentary‑contact button sits over a small spring and two attached wires – the switched (hot) side and the neutral side.  The outer plastic cover is then unscrewed, exposing a metal spring and a small bulb‑like element connected to the wires.  All actions are performed in close‑up on a blue‑gray carpeted surface.

action.detailed: Lift off the front plate of the foot switch, turn the housing over, and unscrew the plastic case to expose the internal button, spring and wiring.

nodes.plm_action: Tighten little screw in middle
nodes.plm_caption: A man's hands are holding a black electrical device. He takes off a spring as he turns it around. He explains what is happening. In the background is a white tray and another of the same device is on it. There is a yellow and silver screwdriver in the tray as well. The lighting is bright and focused on the man's hands.

summary.brief: The presenter removes the spring from a black foot‑switch housing and examines its interior components.
summary.detailed: The video shows the presenter holding a black circular foot‑switch. He turns the housing so the front face is visible, lifts the coiled metal spring that wraps around the central screw and sets the spring aside on the white tray. While the spring is removed he points out the central screw, the black cord that runs through the opening, and a small clear plastic piece inside the switch. The background includes a second identical switch and a yellow‑and‑silver screwdriver on the tray. He then continues to rotate the switch slightly, displaying the wiring and pins before the segment ends.

action.detailed: Rotate the housing, lift the coiled metal spring away from the central screw, place the spring on the tray, and turn the switch to expose its interior components.

nodes.plm_action: Pull out the cable to ensure it is fully seated
nodes.plm_caption:
The video shows the bottom side of a motor to which two wires are attached. The person is touching the wires and explaining what they are for. At the end of the video the person is holding the motor away from the camera. The lighting is good and there are some screwdrivers at the top. It is indoors and seems to be an instructional video.
The hand on the right holds a black circular base for the motor. They keep the base facing the camera until the 6 seconds mark when they turn the base slightly to show more of the underside. At the 8 second mark, their right thumb and forefinger press on the wires extending from the base, and the left hand touches the wire. At the 10 second mark, they release their left hand and use their right hand to pull on the base in an upward motion. At the 13 second mark, they turn the base back to face the camera again. At the 15 second mark, they use their left thumb and forefinger to pull on one of the wires, and their other hand to hold the base in place. The right thumb and forefinger are used to rotate the motor body upward and then away from the camera, at the 24 second mark.
There is a bright rectangle of light on the floor at the very top of the shot, in front of the white rectangular base and screwdriver. To the right of that are some grey metal panels mounted side to side in rows. At the bottom right of the frame is a small area of blue carpet visible behind the right hand.

summary.brief: The presenter examines the foot‑switch base, rotates it to expose the underside, manipulates the wires, and lifts the assembly away.
summary.detailed: The presenter holds the black circular foot‑switch base with the right hand, keeping the front facing the camera. After a few seconds the base is turned slightly to show its underside. The presenter then presses the two wires protruding from the base with the right thumb and forefinger while the left hand touches one of the wires. The left hand releases and the right hand pulls the base upward a short distance, then the base is turned back toward the camera. Next, the left thumb and forefinger pull on one wire while the other hand steadies the base. Finally, the right thumb and forefinger rotate the switch housing upward and pull the whole assembly away from the camera, exposing the internal connections. Screwdrivers rest on a surface above, and the lighting remains bright throughout.

action.detailed: Hold the circular base, rotate it to expose the underside, press and pull the attached wires with thumb and forefinger, lift the base upward, then rotate and pull the assembly away from the camera.
action.actor: The presenter (the person filming the tutorial)

nodes.plm_caption:
A man demonstrates how to install something, showing how to position a tiny tool with a sharp tip. The metal tool has a pair of black plastic cups that it can be moved in. He also points to a cylinder-shaped object in a plastic tube and pulls the tube out of the plastic object. He then takes a tiny metal spike and places it in the black plastic cup.
The plastic object is mostly white, with black parts and a yellow-handled tool lying on top of it. The background is dark gray carpet and the man's white shirt can be seen. The lighting is very dim, with a strong shadow in the top right-hand corner. There is a visible shadow in the bottom left corner.

summary.brief: The demonstrator uses a tiny screwdriver‑like tool to release the wire from a foot‑switch assembly.
summary.detailed: The hands point to the black‑silver foot switch and insert the tip of a very small screwdriver (from an eyeglass‑repair kit) into a tiny release hole on the side of the switch. A small plastic tube is pulled out of the housing, exposing two black plastic cups. A minute metal spike is then placed into one of the cups and pressed down, which frees the copper‑sleeved wire attached to the switch. The wire is then pulled away, completing the disconnection of the switch from the cord.

action.detailed: Insert the thin screwdriver tip into the switch’s release hole, pull the inner plastic tube out, place the metal spike into the black plastic cup, press to disengage the wire, and pull the wire free.

nodes.plm_action: Insert terminal with wire inside into hole in harness
nodes.plm_caption:
A man is holding black wires with plastic containers in the left hand and a small metal tool in the right hand and moving around the wires and container.  The background is a blue and white square box filled with black and plastic objects with a screw driver in it. The lighting is bright and natural.
The man's hands are the only moving object in the frame.

summary.brief: The man works on a black cord with a clear connector, using a metal tip to wiggle the wire and an Allen key to adjust the connector’s screw.
summary.detailed: Holding the black cord and its clear plastic connector in his left hand, the man first uses a small metal tool in his right hand to poke and move the exposed wire, moving the tool up‑down and side‑to‑side so the wire wiggles. He then picks up an Allen‑key‑style tool, inserts it into the screw on the connector, turns it counter‑clockwise to loosen the screw while keeping the cord steady, pulls the cable slightly, and finally turns the key clockwise to tighten the screw again. The background shows a blue‑white tool box containing other screws and a screwdriver.

action.detailed: Insert the Allen key into the screw on the cord’s connector, turn it counter‑clockwise to loosen, reposition the cable as needed, then turn the key clockwise to tighten the screw while holding the cord steady with the other hand.

nodes.plm_action: Remove insulation from wire
nodes.plm_caption: This video features a man working on some sort of electrical device using various tools.

summary.brief: The presenter removes the rubber‑capped metal tube of the foot switch, pulls the black wire out, and then reassembles the connector by inserting the wire, securing it with a screw and tightening the nut.
summary.detailed: First the demonstrator lifts off the rubber cap covering a short metal tube and unscrews the tube from its plastic housing. Using needle‑nose pliers he pulls the black wire out of the tube and examines the exposed conductors. He then places the wire into a small transparent plastic connector, pushes a tiny screw or pin into the connector’s hole and taps it into place with a screwdriver. summary_sent_to_llm.title: Foot switch for floor lamp
summary_sent_to_llm.description: Changing out bad foot switch for a floor lamp
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The hands grasp the foot switch assembly on a floor lamp and begin by unscrewing three of the four mounting screws with a screwdriver, then remove the last screw to free the front cover. The front plate is lifted off, leaving the button in place, and turned upside‑down to expose the internal mechanism, including a spring and the single hot‑side wire that is switched. The lower half of the housing is also opened to show how the hot conductor wraps around a metal clip. Using a tiny screwdriver from an eyeglass‑repair kit, the tip is inserted into a release hole in the clip; the pressure releases the grip on the crimped copper‑sleeved wire, which is then pulled out of the switch. The same release procedure is performed on the opposite side, demonstrating how the switch can be completely removed and later reinstalled by reversing these steps.

Disassemble foot switch and inspect motor base
Disassemble and resecure the switch wiring
